classification.difficultyReason: Convert the stated diameters to radii, combine the areas of two smaller pizzas, and explain why adding diameters does not establish which option provides more pizza.

inlines.text: You order a 9-inch pizza from a restaurant.
After a while, the waiter tells you that they no longer have 9-inch pizza bases and will instead give you two 5-inch pizzas instead.
He tries to convince you, saying that you will get more since
Explain to him why this is not a good deal.
pizza sizes are measured according to the diameter.
Round the final area of the 9-inch pizza and the combined area of the two 5-inch pizzas to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: One 9-inch diameter pizza and two 5-inch diameter pizzas; given diameters marked across each circle.
spec.mathematics: One 9-inch diameter pizza and two 5-inch diameter pizzas; given diameters marked across each circle.
spec.answerVisibility: Given measurements only; unknowns are not evaluated.

answer.short: The 9-inch pizza has area $63.62\text{ in}^2$; the two 5-inch pizzas have combined area $39.27\text{ in}^2$. You receive less pizza, so this is not a good deal. Area depends on the square of the radius, rather than the sum of the diameters.
answer.worked:
9-inch pizza: $r=9\div2=4.5\text{ in}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_9&=\pi r^2\\A_9&=\pi(4.5)^2\\A_9&=20.25\pi\text{ in}^2\\A_9&\approx63.62\text{ in}^2\end{align*}$$
Each 5-inch pizza: $r=5\div2=2.5\text{ in}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{two}}&=2\pi r^2\\A_{\text{two}}&=2\pi(2.5)^2\\A_{\text{two}}&=12.5\pi\text{ in}^2\\A_{\text{two}}&\approx39.27\text{ in}^2\end{align*}$$
Since $12.5\pi<20.25\pi$, the two smaller pizzas provide less pizza. Adding diameters does not compare areas: each area depends on the square of its radius.
